clues.clue: I was the first woman.
clues.concern: The phrase 'first woman' is not used verbatim; it is implied by Genesis 2:18-23 (and 1 Timothy 2:13, 'Adam was first formed, then Eve').

clues.clue: I was made from a rib taken from the man.
The serpent spoke to me in the garden.
I am called the mother of all living.

notes: The answer Eve is clearly correct, and no distractor fits any clue. Sarah is called a mother of nations in Genesis 17:16, but she is not called 'mother of all living.' The explanation accurately quotes Genesis 3:20. It omits the opening 'And' and uses a straight apostrophe, which is acceptable. In Genesis 2-3 the woman is not yet named Eve when she is made or when the serpent speaks to her, but this is standard and not misleading.

clues.clue: My mother laughed when my birth was promised.
My father was a hundred years old when I was born.
I was laid on an altar in the land of Moriah.
clues.concern: The land of Moriah is named in Genesis 22:2. Verse 9 covers the altar but does not name Moriah.

clues.clue: My sons were Esau and Jacob.

notes: All four clues point uniquely to Isaac. Ishmael's father Abraham was 86 at his birth (Genesis 16:16), so the age clue does not fit him. The explanation accurately paraphrases Genesis 22:9. Optionally, cite Genesis 22:2 alongside 22:9 to support the Moriah detail.

clues.clue: I was Abram's nephew.
clues.concern: KJV does not use the word 'nephew'; it calls Lot 'his brother's son' (Genesis 12:5; also Genesis 11:27, 11:31, 14:12), which means the same thing. Laban was the grandson of Abram's brother Nahor, not his nephew, so there is no conflict.

clues.clue: I chose all the plain of Jordan.
Two angels came to my house in Sodom.
clues.concern: Verse 1 says two angels came to Sodom, and verse 3 says they entered Lot's house. Citing the range is best.

clues.clue: My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

notes: The answer and the cited reference are accurate. None of the distractors fit any clue: Terah was Abram's father, Nahor was Abram's brother, and Laban was Nahor's grandson. The explanation closely paraphrases Genesis 19:26. Optional fix: change clue 1 to 'I was the son of Abram's brother' to follow KJV wording.

clues.clue: I am called a soothsayer.
Balak, king of Moab, sent for me to curse Israel.
An angel with a drawn sword stood in my way.
clues.concern: The angel with drawn sword is first mentioned in Numbers 22:23. Verse 31 is where Balaam himself sees it, so either verse works.

clues.clue: My ass spoke to me.

notes: All the clues fit Balaam and none fits Jethro, Balak or Korah. Balak sent for Balaam but was not himself sent for. The soothsayer title comes from Joshua 13:22 ('Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer'). The explanation shortens the ass's quote accurately.

clues.clue: I was a Levite and the brother of Moses.
I spoke to Pharaoh on Moses' behalf.
I made a golden calf when the people asked.
My rod budded and yielded almonds.

notes: All clues fit Aaron and are well supported in the KJV. Moses was also a Levite who spoke to Pharaoh, but the clues 'brother of Moses' and 'on Moses' behalf' exclude him. Eleazar and Joshua do not fit. The explanation accurately paraphrases Numbers 17:8.

clues.clue: I was a priest of Midian.
clues.concern: Also called Reuel/Raguel, the priest of Midian, in Exodus 2:16-18, but the clue is accurate for Jethro.

clues.clue: I was Moses' father-in-law.
clues.concern: Laban was Jacob's father-in-law, not Moses'. No distractor fits this clue.

clues.clue: Moses kept my flock near Horeb.
clues.concern: Laban's flocks were kept by Jacob, but not near Horeb. Not a real conflict.

clues.clue: I advised Moses to appoint rulers to judge the people.

notes: All clues are accurate, and Jethro is clearly the answer. The explanation matches Exodus 3:1. The distractors (Balak, Laban, Aaron) are not priests of Midian and are not Moses' father-in-law. Laban, as a shepherd father-in-law, offers a mild thematic similarity, but no clue actually fits him.

clues.clue: I drew water for a stranger's camels at a well.
clues.concern: Rachel also came to a well with her father's sheep (Genesis 29:9-10), but Jacob watered them, and no camels are involved. The clue fits Rebekah alone.

clues.clue: I was the sister of Laban.
clues.concern: Rachel and Leah were Laban's daughters, not his sisters, so the clue is not ambiguous.

clues.clue: I married Isaac.
I helped my son Jacob receive his father's blessing.

notes: All clues are accurate and point uniquely to Rebekah. The explanation correctly paraphrases Genesis 24:67. The 'stranger' was Abraham's servant (Genesis 24:17-20), which is a fair description. The clue 'sister of Laban' could optionally cite Genesis 25:20 as a further confirmation.

clues.clue: My father was Laban.
clues.concern: Also true of Leah, who is among the options. This clue alone does not distinguish the answer, though the later clues do.

clues.clue: Jacob served seven years for me, and they seemed but a few days.
I was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
I died on the way to Bethlehem.
clues.concern: KJV says she was buried 'in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.' The clue is accurate as a paraphrase.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (father was Laban) also fits Leah. The remaining clues uniquely identify Rachel.
notes: The item is sound. The explanation quotes Genesis 29:20 accurately, slightly abridged (it omits 'for the love he had to her'). Consider putting a more distinctive clue first, or accept the Leah overlap as a deliberate opening red herring.

clues.clue: I was a priest at Shiloh.
clues.concern: Samuel ministered at Shiloh too, but he was not described as the priest there; 1 Samuel 1:3 also places Eli's sons as priests at Shiloh. Minor issue.

clues.clue: I thought Hannah was drunken as she prayed.
My sons Hophni and Phinehas were wicked.
clues.concern: The names come from 1 Samuel 1:3 and 2:34. Verse 2:12 calls them 'sons of Belial', which supports 'wicked'.

clues.clue: I fell backward and died when I heard the ark was taken.

notes: The answer and explanation are accurate. Samuel ministered at Shiloh under Eli, but the other clues exclude him. The hint 'books of history' is acceptable.

clues.clue: I was the son of King Saul.
clues.concern: Accurate, but it also fits the distractor Ishbosheth, who is called 'Ishbosheth the son of Saul' (2 Samuel 2:8). The other clues still single out Jonathan.

clues.clue: I climbed up to a Philistine garrison with my armourbearer.
My soul was knit with the soul of David.
I warned David by shooting arrows.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('son of King Saul') also fits Ishbosheth (2 Samuel 2:8). Clues 2-4 apply only to Jonathan.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate for 1 Samuel 18:1. Consider making clue 1 more specific (e.g., 'I was Saul's eldest son', 1 Samuel 14:49 lists Jonathan first) or ordering clues so the first is not shared with a distractor. The arrow signal was planned in 1 Samuel 20:20-22 and carried out in 20:35-39.

clues.clue: I was a champion of the Philistines.
I came from Gath.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Achish, king of Gath (1 Samuel 21:10; 27:2). The other clues settle the answer, so this is a minor issue.

clues.clue: My height was six cubits and a span.
A shepherd boy struck me down with a sling and a stone.
clues.concern: The KJV calls David a 'youth' (17:33, 42) who kept sheep (17:34), so 'shepherd boy' is a fair paraphrase. The stone felled Goliath, but David then killed him with Goliath's own sword (17:51). 'Struck me down' is still accurate.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 ('I came from Gath') alone also fits Achish, king of Gath. No other clue fits him, so the combined clues still point uniquely to Goliath.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate to 1 Samuel 17:4. Og was also a giant (Deuteronomy 3:11) but was an Amorite king of Bashan, not a Philistine. Sisera was Jabin's captain and was killed by Jael. Difficulty 1 is appropriate.

clues.clue: I was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
King David saw me from the roof of his house.
clues.concern: Minor wording issue: the KJV says David, walking on the roof of the king's house, 'saw a woman washing herself.' David was on the roof, not Bathsheba. The clue reads correctly but could be misread as Bathsheba being on the roof.

clues.clue: I became the mother of Solomon.
My son King Solomon set a seat for me at his right hand.

notes: All clues uniquely fit Bathsheba. Michal was Saul's daughter and David's wife. Tamar was David's daughter, or Judah's daughter-in-law. Abigail was Nabal's widow and later David's wife. The explanation accurately reflects 2 Samuel 11:3. The hint 'Look in 2 Samuel' is fine, though the final clue comes from 1 Kings 2:19.

clues.clue: I was a prophet in David's court.
clues.concern: Clue 1 also fits Gad, called "the prophet Gad, David's seer" (2 Samuel 24:11; cf. 1 Samuel 22:5). Later clues settle it, so this only weakens the opening clue.

clues.clue: I told David his son would build God's house.
I told David a parable about a poor man's ewe lamb.
I said to David, Thou art the man.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 also fits the distractor Gad, who was David's prophet and seer (2 Samuel 24:11). Clues 2-4 apply only to Nathan.
notes: The answer Nathan is correct, and the explanation matches 2 Samuel 12:7. The hint is accurate. Consider making clue 1 more specific, e.g. "I was the prophet to whom David spoke of building a house for the ark." Clue 2 is paralleled in 1 Chronicles 17:11-12.

clues.clue: I was a king of Israel.
clues.concern: Generic: also true of Jeroboam, Omri, and Jehu. This is acceptable as an opening clue because the later clues are unique to Ahab.

clues.clue: I married Jezebel.
I asked Elijah, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
I wanted Naboth's vineyard for a garden of herbs.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (king of Israel) also fits Jeroboam, Omri, and Jehu. The remaining clues uniquely identify Ahab, so the item is not ambiguous overall.
notes: The quotations match the KJV. The explanation accurately reflects 1 Kings 21:2.

clues.clue: I was a son of King David.
clues.concern: Applies equally to all four options (Amnon, Adonijah, Solomon are also David's sons). This is acceptable as an opening clue but does not discriminate on its own.

clues.clue: I stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
I led a rebellion against my father.
clues.concern: Adonijah also exalted himself, saying 'I will be king,' while David was still alive (1 Kings 1:5). That could partially be argued as acting against his father, though Scripture does not describe it as an armed rebellion like Absalom's. This is minor.

clues.clue: My head caught in an oak as my mule went on.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 fits all options. Clue 3 could loosely be argued for Adonijah (1 Kings 1:5), but clues 2 and 4 uniquely identify Absalom.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate to the 2 Samuel 18:9 KJV text. The item is solid overall. Optionally, clue 3 could be sharpened, e.g. 'I made myself king in Hebron' (2 Samuel 15:10).

clues.clue: I was the daughter of the king of the Zidonians.
I was the wife of King Ahab.
I threatened Elijah's life after Mount Carmel.
I arranged Naboth's death to take his vineyard.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely fit Jezebel. Athaliah was Ahab's daughter and the wife of Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8:18, 26), not Ahab's wife, so she does not fit clue 2. The explanation correctly summarizes 1 Kings 19:2.

clues.clue: I was a king of Judah.
clues.concern: Fits all four options (Josiah, Manasseh and Uzziah were also kings of Judah); acceptable only as an opening clue.

clues.clue: I broke in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.
Isaiah told me to set my house in order.
clues.concern: Also in Isaiah 38:1.

clues.clue: God added fifteen years to my life.
clues.concern: Also in 2 Kings 20:6.

notes: The first clue is generic, but the later clues uniquely identify Hezekiah. Josiah also destroyed idolatrous objects (2 Kings 23), but not the brasen serpent. The explanation accurately quotes Isaiah 38:5.

clues.clue: I became king of Judah at eight years old.
The book of the law was found in the temple in my reign.
I rent my clothes when it was read to me.
I kept a great passover.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Hezekiah, who kept a great passover (2 Chronicles 30:1-26, esp. v.26). The other clues still single out Josiah.

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 (great passover) also fits Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 30:26). The combined clues uniquely identify Josiah. Joash began to reign at seven, not eight (2 Kings 11:21), so clue 1 does not fit him.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate. The quote matches 2 Kings 22:1 KJV. Consider making clue 4 more specific to Josiah, e.g. 'no such passover since the days of the judges' (2 Kings 23:22), to reduce overlap with Hezekiah. Jehoiakim is a good contrast distractor, since he burned the scroll and did not rend his clothes (Jeremiah 36:23-24).

clues.clue: I was a priest of the course of Abia.
An angel appeared to me by the altar of incense.
clues.concern: KJV says the angel stood 'on the right side of the altar of incense'; 'by the altar' is an acceptable paraphrase.

clues.clue: I was struck dumb because I did not believe.
I wrote: His name is John.

notes: All clues fit Zacharias uniquely. Joseph (husband of Mary), Annas (high priest) and Simeon (in the temple, Luke 2) do not match any clue. Simeon is in the temple but is not called a priest and saw no angel at the altar. The explanation accurately reflects Luke 1:63.

clues.clue: I was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
I was a gatherer of sycomore fruit.
I said I was no prophet, neither a prophet's son.
clues.concern: Minor wording difference: KJV reads "neither was I a prophet's son"; the meaning is preserved.

clues.clue: I cried: let judgment run down as waters.
clues.concern: Paraphrase: KJV reads "But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream." The text does not say Amos "cried" it, but it is his oracle, so this is acceptable.

notes: The answer is correct, and every clue applies uniquely to Amos. Micah was a Morasthite (Micah 1:1), and no comparable details are given for Obadiah or Hosea. The explanation quotes Amos 7:14 accurately, with ellipses. The clues are quite identifying for difficulty 4. The Tekoa clue in particular is very direct, though the difficulty rating is fine.

clues.clue: I was a priest among the captives by the river Chebar.
I saw wheels whose rings were full of eyes.
I lay on my side for many days as a sign.
I prophesied to a valley of dry bones.

notes: All clues accurately reflect the KJV text of Ezekiel. Ezekiel 1:3 names him a priest by the river Chebar, and Ezekiel 1:1 places him among the captives. Ezekiel 1:18 describes the rings full of eyes. In Ezekiel 4:4-6 he lies 390 days on his left side and 40 days on his right. In Ezekiel 37:1-4 he prophesies to the dry bones. None of the clues fits Jeremiah, Daniel, or Zechariah. Zechariah's visions involve horses, candlesticks, and a flying roll, but not these wheels. Jeremiah was also a priest, but he was not at Chebar. The explanation quotes Ezekiel 37:4 accurately. The hint 'Major Prophets' also applies to Jeremiah and to Daniel (in the English canon), so it narrows the choices only partly, but that is acceptable.

clues.clue: I was of the daughters of Aaron.
I was barren and well stricken in years.
clues.concern: Luke 1:7 says 'Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years,' so it is accurate. Barrenness in old age also fits other biblical women such as Sarah, but none of them are options.

clues.clue: My babe leaped in my womb when Mary greeted me.
I was the mother of John the Baptist.
clues.concern: This clue gives the answer away completely. It is accurate, since Luke 1:13 and 1:57-63 establish it.

notes: The answer is correct. Anna (Luke 2:36) was of the tribe of Aser, not a daughter of Aaron. Salome and Mary do not fit the clues. The explanation accurately reflects Luke 1:41.

clues.clue: I was a priest and a ready scribe in the law of Moses.
clues.concern: Ezra 7:6 calls him 'a ready scribe in the law of Moses'; his priesthood is shown by the Aaronic genealogy in Ezra 7:1-5 and by the title 'Ezra the priest, the scribe' in Ezra 7:11.

clues.clue: I went up from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes.
clues.concern: Nehemiah also went to Jerusalem in Artaxerxes' reign (Nehemiah 2:1-11), but he left from Shushan, not Babylon. Zerubbabel went up from Babylon, but under Cyrus. So the clue still points uniquely to Ezra.

clues.clue: I read the book of the law to the people.
clues.concern: Nehemiah 8:8 says 'they read', meaning Ezra with the Levites, but verses 2-3 name Ezra specifically.

clues.clue: I stood upon a pulpit of wood.

notes: The item is accurate and the marked answer, Ezra, is correct. There is minor overlap with Nehemiah, who also traveled under Artaxerxes, but the phrase 'from Babylon' distinguishes Ezra. The hint is vague but acceptable.

clues.clue: I was of the house and lineage of David.
An angel told me in a dream not to fear to take Mary as my wife.
I took the young child and his mother into Egypt by night.
People called Jesus the carpenter's son.
clues.concern: The clue shifts out of first-person self-description, but it is accurate and points clearly to Joseph.

notes: The answer is correct. Every clue is directly supported by the KJV text. None of the distractors fit: Joseph of Arimathaea, Zacharias, and Simeon match none of the clues. The explanation quotes Matthew 1:20 accurately. The hint 'Look in Matthew' is appropriate, though clue 1 is best supported by Luke 2:4; Matthew 1:20 ('thou son of David') also partially supports it.

clues.clue: I was a prophetess of the tribe of Aser.
I was a widow of about fourscore and four years.
clues.concern: The KJV wording is ambiguous: it may mean she was 84 years old, or that she had been a widow for about 84 years. The clue mirrors the KJV phrasing, so this is acceptable.

clues.clue: I served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
I gave thanks when the child Jesus was brought to the temple.
clues.concern: Luke 2:38 says she 'gave thanks likewise unto the Lord' at that instant, after Simeon's blessing in the temple. This is supported by context.

notes: All clues are drawn directly from Luke 2:36-38, and Anna is correct. No distractor fits. Elisabeth was 'of the daughters of Aaron' (Luke 1:5), not of Aser. Phebe and Dorcas are unrelated to these clues. The explanation accurately quotes Luke 2:36. The reference label could optionally be broadened to Luke 2:36-38 to cover all clues.

clues.clue: I was a just and devout man in Jerusalem.
clues.concern: Partial overlap: Joseph of Arimathaea is called 'a good man, and a just' (Luke 23:50), but 'devout' and 'in Jerusalem' together fit only Simeon. Later clues remove any ambiguity.

clues.clue: The Holy Ghost revealed I would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ.
I took the child Jesus up in my arms in the temple.
I said: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.

notes: All clues are accurate to KJV Luke 2:25-29. The first clue is mildly reminiscent of Joseph of Arimathaea ('just', Luke 23:50) and Zacharias ('righteous', Luke 1:6), but that is not a real conflict. The explanation quotes Luke 2:29 accurately.

clues.clue: I was a prophet to Israel.
clues.concern: Generic. Amos was also explicitly sent to prophesy to Israel (Amos 7:15), and Micah prophesied concerning Samaria (Micah 1:1). This clue alone does not distinguish Hosea from the distractors, though the later clues do.

clues.clue: God told me to marry Gomer.
clues.concern: Slight overstatement. In Hosea 1:2 God commands Hosea to 'take unto thee a wife of whoredoms' but does not name Gomer. Gomer is named only in 1:3, when Hosea obeys.

clues.clue: I named a son Lo-ammi.
clues.concern: The KJV spells the name 'Loammi' (no hyphen). God gave the command to name him, and Hosea carried it out. The clue is acceptable.

clues.clue: I bought my wife back for fifteen pieces of silver.
clues.concern: The clue is incomplete: the price also included 'an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley' (Hosea 3:2). The text says 'a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress' and never explicitly names her as Gomer or calls her his wife. Reading 'bought back my wife' is a common interpretation but is not stated in the text.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('prophet to Israel') also fits Amos (Amos 7:15) and arguably Micah. Clues 2-4 uniquely identify Hosea.
notes: The answer Hosea is correct. The explanation accurately reflects Hosea 1:3. Suggested refinements: reword clue 2 to 'I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim', use the KJV spelling 'Loammi', and reword clue 4 to 'I bought a woman for fifteen pieces of silver and an homer and a half of barley' to avoid the interpretive 'my wife back'. Clue 1 is weak because it also fits Amos. A difficulty rating of 4 seems high given the well-known Gomer clue.

clues.clue: I was from Cana of Galilee.
I asked: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
Jesus saw me under the fig tree.
Jesus called me an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. John 21:2 explicitly says 'Nathanael of Cana in Galilee'. Philip appears in the same passage (John 1:43-48) and is from Bethsaida (John 1:44), so he does not fit. Thomas also appears in John 21:2, but the 'of Cana' description applies only to Nathanael. Clue 1 makes a weak opening clue, since it comes only from John 21:2, but it is correct.

clues.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clues.concern: The same verse says Bethsaida was 'the city of Andrew and Peter,' so this clue also fits the distractor Andrew.

clues.clue: Jesus said to me, Follow me.
clues.concern: Jesus also said 'Follow me' to Andrew (with Peter) in Matthew 4:19 and Mark 1:17, so this clue does not single out Philip on its own.

clues.clue: I told Nathanael: Come and see.
I asked Jesus: Lord, shew us the Father.

distractor_conflict: Clues 1 and 2 also fit Andrew. He was of Bethsaida (John 1:44), and Jesus said 'Follow me' to him and Peter (Matthew 4:19). Clues 3 and 4 identify only Philip.
notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation quotes John 14:8 accurately. Taken together, the clues identify Philip uniquely. The first two clues are weak and fit Andrew too. Consider rewording clue 2 to something specific to Philip, such as 'Jesus findeth me and said, Follow me' (John 1:43), or putting the more specific clues earlier. Nathanael is traditionally identified with Bartholomew, but that does not cause a conflict here.

clues.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clues.concern: This verse names Philip as 'of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter', so the clue fits the distractor Philip equally well (see also John 12:21). It does not distinguish Andrew.

clues.clue: I first heard John the Baptist speak about Jesus.
clues.concern: Supported by John 1:35-40. The wording 'first heard' is slightly awkward. Two disciples heard John, and the other is unnamed, so this does not uniquely identify Andrew, though no distractor is named there.

clues.clue: I brought my brother Simon to Jesus.
I found a lad with five barley loaves.
clues.concern: The KJV has Andrew saying 'There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves'. It never says Andrew 'found' the lad, so the clue overstates the text. Rephrase to 'I told Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves.'

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (from Bethsaida) also fits Philip, who John 1:44 explicitly says was of Bethsaida.
notes: Andrew is the correct answer, and the combined clues identify him uniquely. The explanation accurately reflects John 1:41-42, though the cited label is John 1:40-41 and the 'brought him to Jesus' part is in verse 42. Suggested fixes: reword clue 1 (e.g. 'I shared a hometown with Peter and Philip') or accept that it is a non-distinguishing clue, and change 'found' in clue 4 to 'told Jesus of'.

clues.clue: I lived in Joppa.
I was full of good works and almsdeeds.
I made coats and garments that the widows showed.
clues.concern: Slight paraphrase: the widows showed the coats and garments Dorcas made 'while she was with them'. Accurate.

clues.clue: Peter said to me, arise, and I opened my eyes.

notes: All clues are well supported by Acts 9:36-40. None of the distractors fit: Lydia was of Thyatira and lived in Philippi, Priscilla is linked with Corinth, Ephesus and Rome, and Phebe with Cenchrea. The first clue identifies her outright, so the item is fairly easy, but it is still valid.

clues.clue: I was the Roman governor of Judaea.
clues.concern: Felix was also a Roman governor over Judaea (Acts 23:24-26; Acts 24:27), so this clue alone also fits the distractor Felix. The later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: My wife sent word about a dream concerning a just man.
I asked: What is truth?
I washed my hands before the multitude.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('Roman governor of Judaea') also fits Felix, who is called governor in Acts 23:24-26 and Acts 24:27. The remaining clues uniquely identify Pilate.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate to Matthew 27:24. Consider making clue 1 more specific, e.g. 'governor of Judaea in the fifteenth year of Tiberius' (Luke 3:1), to avoid overlap with Felix. The word 'Roman' is not explicit in the KJV but is a fair inference.

clues.clue: I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law.
I was had in reputation among all the people.
I told the council to let the apostles alone.
Paul was brought up at my feet.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. Acts 5:34 supports the first two clues. Acts 5:38 reads 'Refrain from these men, and let them alone.' Acts 22:3 reads 'brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.' Nicodemus was also a Pharisee and a ruler (John 3:1), but he is never called a doctor of the law. None of the other clues fit him, so the first clue alone may give a little early ambiguity but there is no real conflict. Caiaphas was high priest and is not described as a Pharisee. Ananias does not fit any clue.

clues.clue: I was high priest that same year.
clues.concern: Annas is also called high priest (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6; John 18:19-22), but the phrase 'that same year' is used only of Caiaphas (John 11:49, 51; 18:13).

clues.clue: I said it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
clues.concern: Also recalled in John 18:14.

clues.clue: Annas was my father-in-law.
Jesus was led bound to me after His arrest.
clues.concern: Partly fits the distractor Annas. In John 18:12-13 Jesus was bound and led to Annas first. Annas then sent Him bound to Caiaphas (John 18:24; cf. Matthew 26:57). Suggested rewording: 'Annas sent Jesus to me bound.'

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 also fits Annas, since Jesus was bound and led 'to Annas first' (John 18:12-13). Clue 1's 'high priest' could loosely suggest Annas (Luke 3:2; Acts 4:6), though 'that same year' points to Caiaphas. Taken together, the clues still identify Caiaphas uniquely.
notes: The answer Caiaphas is correct. The explanation accurately reflects John 11:49-50, and ref_kjv matches the KJV text. The minor issue is clue 4: the arresting party led Jesus bound to Annas first, so the clue should be reworded to reflect John 18:24 ('Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas'). That would remove the overlap with the Annas option.

clues.clue: My husband Aquila and I were tentmakers.
clues.concern: Acts 18:2-3 names Aquila with his wife Priscilla, and verse 3 says 'by their occupation they were tentmakers.' The plural 'they' includes Paul and the couple, so Priscilla's inclusion is a reasonable reading but not explicitly certain.

clues.clue: We came from Italy when Claudius commanded the Jews to leave Rome.
Paul stayed and worked with us in Corinth.
clues.concern: Acts 18:1-3 places this in Corinth: Paul 'abode with them, and wrought.'

clues.clue: We expounded the way of God more perfectly to Apollos.
clues.concern: The meeting took place in Ephesus (Acts 18:24), not Corinth. The clue does not state a location, so it is not inaccurate.

notes: Priscilla is the correct answer, and none of the clues fits Dorcas, Lydia or Phebe. The explanation matches Acts 18:26. Lydia was a seller of purple, not a tentmaker. One minor point: the first clue relies on the plural 'they' in Acts 18:3, so the verse does not explicitly confirm that Priscilla herself was a tentmaker.

clues.clue: I was a centurion of the Italian band.
I was a devout man who prayed to God alway.
An angel told me to send to Joppa for Peter.
The Holy Ghost fell on my household while Peter spoke.
clues.concern: Slightly imprecise: KJV says the Holy Ghost 'fell on all them which heard the word,' which included Cornelius's kinsmen and near friends (Acts 10:24), not only his household. Acceptable but could read 'on all who heard.'

notes: Answer is correct and unambiguous. Julius was also a centurion, but of 'Augustus' band' (Acts 27:1), so clue 1 excludes him. Claudius Lysias was a chief captain (Acts 23:26), and Sergius Paulus was a deputy/proconsul (Acts 13:7). Explanation matches Acts 10:1. Consider rewording clue 4 for precision.

clues.clue: I was a Jew born at Alexandria.
I was an eloquent man, mighty in the scriptures.
Aquila and Priscilla taught me the way of God more perfectly.
clues.concern: KJV gives the order 'Aquila and Priscilla' and says they 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly'. 'Taught' is a fair paraphrase. Including Aquila's name in the clue gives a mild hint against the Aquila distractor but does not make it fit.

clues.clue: Paul wrote that he planted and I watered.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV and point uniquely to Apollos. None of the clues fits Titus, Silas, or Aquila. The explanation matches Acts 18:24. The difficulty of 4 may be generous given the clues are well known, but that is acceptable.

clues.clue: I was a chief man among the brethren.
clues.concern: Judas surnamed Barsabas is also called a chief man in the same verse, but he is not an option.

clues.clue: I travelled with Paul after he parted from Barnabas.
clues.concern: On its own this also loosely fits Timothy, who joined Paul soon after (Acts 16:1-3), and Luke, whose 'we' passages begin at Acts 16:10. Only Silas was chosen at the parting itself.

clues.clue: I was beaten and put in the stocks with Paul at Philippi.
At midnight Paul and I prayed and sang praises.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 by itself could loosely apply to Timothy (Acts 16:1-3) or Luke (Acts 16:10), who also travelled with Paul after the split from Barnabas. Taken together, the clues point only to Silas.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation matches Acts 16:25 KJV. Rewording clue 2 to 'Paul chose me when he parted from Barnabas' would make it uniquely fit Silas.

clues.clue: I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
Sisera fled to my tent.
I gave him milk when he asked for water.
I drove a nail of the tent into his temples.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. Judges 4:17 says Sisera 'fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite.' Judges 4:19 records that he asked for water and she 'opened a bottle of milk' (also Judges 5:25). Judges 4:21 matches the explanation. No distractor fits: Deborah appears in the same narrative but did none of these acts, and Rahab and Delilah are unrelated. The hint is fine.

clues.clue: I was king in Judaea when Jesus was born.
clues.concern: Verse says 'in the days of Herod the king' with Jesus born in Bethlehem of Judaea; Luke 1:5 explicitly calls him 'Herod, the king of Judaea.' Accurate.

clues.clue: I was troubled when wise men asked for the King of the Jews.
I told the wise men to bring me word again.
I ordered the children in Bethlehem slain.
clues.concern: Minor: the slaughter also covered 'all the coasts thereof,' children two years old and under. Not inaccurate.

notes: Answer is correct. Archelaus reigned in Judaea only after Herod's death (Matthew 2:22), so no clue fits him. Augustus was emperor, not king in Judaea (Luke 2:1). Pilate was governor much later. The explanation accurately paraphrases Matthew 2:16. Optionally, the explanation could identify him as 'Herod the king' (the Great) to distinguish him from Herod Antipas, but the clues already disambiguate.

clues.clue: My husband Nabal was churlish.
I brought bread, wine and figs to David's men.
clues.concern: The list is partial: the gift also included five sheep, parched corn, and raisins. Verse 27 confirms it was for the young men who followed David. The clue is still accurate.

clues.clue: I persuaded David not to shed blood.
After Nabal died, I became David's wife.
clues.concern: Taken alone, 'became David's wife after my husband died' would also describe Bathsheba (after Uriah). Naming Nabal removes the ambiguity.

notes: The marked answer, Abigail, is correct and well supported by 1 Samuel 25. The explanation accurately paraphrases 1 Samuel 25:3. None of the distractors fit the clues once Nabal is named. Ahinoam is mentioned as David's wife in 25:43, but she has no connection to Nabal.

clues.clue: I lived in the valley of Sorek.
The lords of the Philistines offered me silver.
I asked a strong man the secret of his strength.
I had his seven locks shaved while he slept.
clues.concern: Minor: KJV says she made him sleep upon her knees and called for a man to shave off the seven locks. 'While he slept' is accurate.

notes: Accurate item. No distractor fits: Jezebel, Jael and Michal have no connection to Sorek, Philistine silver or Samson. Michal did deceive Saul's messengers to protect David (1 Samuel 19), but that does not match these clues. The explanation adds 'Samson' where the verse says 'he', which is supported by the context.
